findings.text: The kcore facility exposes a permanent proc entry that presents physical and virtual memory as a core dump image. Creation binds a proc operations table designating handlers for iterated read plus open plus release plus seek. Open and release manage a per open bounce area while the read handler serves header plus program headers plus notes plus memory contents.

The ram inventory is rebuilt by discovering the highest node end and scanning system ram through a callback. The callback ignores invalid frames, allocates an entry sized from the page count, derives a direct map address, discards unmappable results, trims address overflow and overlap with the vmalloc region, tags the entry as ram, queues it, and allows a sparsemem helper to veto the entry.

Ram refresh moves through staging to commit to reclaim. Under exclusive access it tests and clears a pending flag, builds a fresh collection, re arms the flag and discards the staging collection on failure, otherwise retires prior ram and vmemmap nodes to a garbage collection, attaches the fresh collection, refreshes total length, releases exclusive access, then destroys garbage outside the lock.

All list mutation and whole file reads serialize on a single percpu reader writer control. Refresh takes the write side, the iterated read path takes the read side for its entire duration, and inode size synchronization uses the inode mutex. The pending flag is exchanged while holding the write side so concurrent refresh requests coalesce.

The byte stream begins with a core type header, continues with a note program header plus one load header per tracked range, continues with a note segment, then exposes range contents. Each load header is marked readable writable executable and page aligned, with file position derived from virtual position plus a data base, virtual position equal to the tracked address, sizes equal to the tracked length, and physical position varying by range kind.

The note segment aggregates four descriptors covering process status, process info, current task structure, and vmcoreinfo. Process info carries a running marker and a kernel image name plus the saved command line. Each note stores name length with terminator plus descriptor length plus type, with padding to a four byte boundary after name and after descriptor, and vmcoreinfo length is bounded by remaining note space.

Data reads resolve the current file position to a tracked range or return zeros when unmapped. Vmalloc ranges use a safe iterator with write fault handling and retry, user ranges use direct copy, ram ranges are skipped with zeros when the frame is absent or offline or poisoned or excluded or unaccepted, otherwise ram uses device memory translation and other kernel ranges use direct addressing through a fault tolerant bounce copy with zero fill on failure, while unknown range kinds log once and read as zeros.

The read path freezes page offline activity while holding read access and periodically thaws to allow scheduling before refreezing, preventing starvation of offline drivers. Freeze and read protection are always released on exit including error paths, so a failed copy does not leave the machine frozen or locked.

Opening kcore enforces a lockdown check and a raw input output privilege check, allocates a page sized per file buffer, opportunistically refreshes the ram inventory when flagged, and aligns the inode length with the current proc length under the inode mutex. Release frees the per file buffer and reports success.

Startup registers text plus vmalloc plus optional modules plus ram and then subscribes to memory hotplug. Text registration and modules registration each have an active and an empty build variant, with modules registered only when the module span differs from the vmalloc span. The hotplug handler requests a refresh on online and offline events and reports successful handling.

Each tracked range carries a virtual address plus a byte length plus a kind tag plus list linkage. Observed kinds distinguish ram and vmemmap and vmalloc and kernel text and user memory. Three static instances represent the vmalloc span and the kernel text span and the modules span.

The kmsg facility exposes a permanent proc entry for the kernel log with handlers for read plus poll plus open plus release plus seek. Open and release delegate to syslog open and close from proc context, read reports would block when nonblocking with no unread data and otherwise delegates to syslog read, poll waits on the log wait queue and signals readability when unread data exists.

Load average and memory info are each exposed as permanent single shot proc entries whose show routine formats kernel state. The load routine samples three averages and reports running and thread counts plus a pid cursor. The memory routine combines system info plus committed memory plus cache plus per list page counts plus slab plus stack plus table plus vmalloc plus balloon plus graphics plus huge page plus memtest plus architecture details.

Memory values are rendered as kilobytes with fixed width labels, converting page counts to kilobyte units. A core set of rows is always emitted while high memory plus no mmu plus compressed swap plus shadow stack plus poisoned pages plus huge pages plus contiguous reserve plus unaccepted memory add conditional rows, and a small set of legacy rows is always reported as zero.

Architecture specific memory reporting is provided through a weak default hook invoked at the end of the memory display. The default implementation produces no output and may be overridden by architecture code.

Namespace support centers on a table of per type operations whose membership depends on build options, always including mount handling. Link inodes bind readlink plus follow plus a no permission change attribute handler. Instantiation creates a world accessible link inode, attaches the per type operations, refreshes identity from the target task, and splices with pid dentry handling.

Namespace link follow and readlink both resolve the owning task, acquire the killable read side of the execution update lock, enforce read access under file system credentials, then either jump to the namespace path or copy the textual name to user space. The lock is released and the task reference dropped on every exit, with distinct failures for missing context and denied access.
The namespace directory listing first emits dot entries and then walks the operations table starting from the current position offset, terminating when the position moves past the end of the table.

Proc entry names and creation modes are fixed. The core dump image and kernel log use owner read access while load average and memory info are created with no extra mode bits and later marked permanent.

The core image uses core file type with current version and architecture specific machine and flags, program header sizes matching header structures, a leading note header plus trailing load headers, and note types for process status plus process info plus task structure plus vmcoreinfo.
